summary.text: A language model failure with a stable machine-readable code.
Identifies the failure independently of its human-readable message.

A local language model conversation. One generation may run at a time.
Always dispose a session when its owning screen or task ends.
Capabilities of the selected provider. Compatibility never changes native support flags.

Aborts pending generation and tool callbacks and releases the native session.
Repeated calls are harmless. Already-started tool effects cannot be undone.
Generates and validates a complete structured result.
Generates a complete text response. Failures reject rather than returning partial success.
Streams full text snapshots followed by exactly one validated result. Breaking iteration aborts generation.
Streams text snapshots. Tool and generation failures throw from the iterator.
Bounds the number of items in an array.
Support for a feature on the currently selected provider and model.
Options for selecting exactly one of the supplied categories.
Distinct, nonempty category labels. The result is one of these exact strings.
Options for one independent plain text task.

Text events are complete snapshots. Structured snapshots are raw text until
the final result validates; partially parsed objects are not exposed yet.
A complete successful result. Validation checks structure, not factual accuracy.
Unknown measurements remain null rather than being estimated.
A provisional, cumulative text snapshot. Replace the previous preview.
Options shared by one-shot requests.
Receives provisional full text snapshots; the promise provides the validated final result.
Provider-reported token counts. Unknown measurements are null; optional fields are omitted when unavailable.
Cached tokens included in inputTokens, when reported by the provider.
Tokens in the final model call's completed context. This is not billed or per-request input usage.
Reasoning tokens included in outputTokens, when reported by the provider.
An app-provided image file. Network and data URLs are not accepted.
Unique within the request, 1–128 characters without control characters. Tools refer to this label.
Stable failure codes shared by preparation, sessions, and one-shot tasks.
Readiness of the requested local model. Checking readiness never starts a download.
Availability is provider- and model-specific, not an OS-version guarantee.
Native OCR and barcode tools for labeled local images. Omitted by older providers.
Requirements are checked during availability, preparation, and session creation.
Explicit language support requirements. Android currently reports language-support-unknown when supplied.
Explicit output language requirement. Omit on Android while support cannot be verified.
Selects the system provider. Downloadable third-party backends are not included.

The supported JSON Schema subset. Unknown keywords reject before generation.
Objects are closed. Required fields must name declared properties. Numeric
bounds are inclusive. Null, unions, references, and string patterns are not
supported yet.
Inclusively bounds a numeric value.
A closed object schema used for tool arguments.
Controls one generation and all model/tool work it initiates.
Return true to allow a validated tool call, or false to end the generation without executing it.
Local image files. Up to 8; labels default to image-1, image-2, and so on. Apple image tools support iOS 26; model vision requires iOS 27 and model support.
Maximum output tokens per model call. Unsupported explicit options reject.
Maximum additional library validation repair attempts per response; integers 0–3, default 1. Does not select a weaker implementation. Provider failures and tool handlers are never retried.
Maximum library model calls, including repairs; integers 1–32. Compatibility loops default to 8. Rejects with native tools because their internal model calls cannot be counted.
Maximum handler starts. Defaults to 4; integers 0–16. Applies to native and compatibility tools.
Optional overall deadline in milliseconds, including tool handlers and approval. No library deadline applies when omitted.
Describes a schema value to the model.
Options used to create a session.
Options for one independent task with a final schema-validated value.
A request for a final schema-validated value.
Options for summarizing text in an independent task.
Relative summary length. Defaults to medium; this is a model preference, not a size guarantee.
Plain text requests cannot contain structured generation options.
Complete, validated arguments supplied to the application's action interceptor.
A tool handler's request identity and cooperative cancellation signal.

Optional helpers for the supported JSON Schema dialect. Objects are closed
and properties are required unless wrapped in
`schema.optional(...)`

.
Helpers preserve literal types without
`as const`

. Supported plain JSON
schemas can also be used directly or combined with helpers. See the schema
helper reference for supported methods and options.

Assigns text to one supplied category and validates the selected label.
Uses native constrained output when available, otherwise validates generated
output with bounded repair attempts. Invalid categories never return as success.

Creates a session using the on-device system model. Rejects when the
requirements are unmet. Does not request model preparation or select a cloud
provider. On Web, browser-managed assets can change after the readiness check.
Tools use native orchestration when supported, otherwise a bounded library loop.

Performs one independent task and validates the result against a schema.
Uses native constrained output when available, otherwise validates generated
output with bounded repair attempts. Provider failures do not trigger fallback.

Checks whether the requested system model is ready, without starting a download.
Apple Intelligence must be enabled and its system model ready on supported hardware.
Availability can change; callers must also handle generation failures.
Android requires supported Gemini Nano hardware and ML Kit model readiness.
Web support depends on the browser's local Prompt API and model readiness.

Explicitly prepares a system model. Android downloads require allowDownload: true
and a foreground app. Progress is a fraction from 0 to 1, or null when unknown.
Cancellation stops this request's work; it does not remove shared model assets.
Apple manages model preparation through system settings; this adapter cannot
trigger its download or report progress, even when allowDownload is true.
Browser model assets are managed by the browser; Web preparation requires a
user gesture when it needs to create the browser model.

Summarizes text using the same generation, tool, update, and cancellation behavior as generateAsync.
Each call owns an independent session. Summary length is a generation preference.
